title: Fluorescence-quenching of a Liposomal-encapsulated Near-infrared Fluorophore as a Tool for In Vivo Optical Imaging
protocol: Dissolve egg phosphatidylcholine (EPC), cholesterol, mPEG2000-DSPE, and NBD-DOPE in chloroform to prepare stock solutions.

Transfer the appropriate volume of phospholipid stock solution into a round bottom flask containing 3 ml chloroform to achieve a liposome composition of EPC:Chol:mPEG2000-DSPE at a molar ratio of 6.5:3:0.5 with 0.3 mol% NBD-DOPE.
Evaporate the chloroform from the phospholipid solution under reduced pressure (300 mbar) at 55 °C using a rotary evaporator.
Reduce the pressure to 10 mbar for 1-2 hours to remove residual chloroform deposits.
Dissolve DY-676-COOH in 10 mM Tris buffer pH 7.4.

Transfer an appropriate volume (0.5–1 ml) of DY-676-COOH (6.181 µM) solution to the round bottom flask to hydrate the dry phospholipid film and vortex vigorously until a spontaneously formed vesicle dispersion forms.
Carefully transfer the round bottom flask containing the SFV dispersion into liquid nitrogen and freeze the dispersion for 3–5 min.
Place the round bottom flask into an ultrasonic bath at 50 °C to thaw the dispersion then vortex the dispersion vigorously for 1–2 min.
Repeat freezing and thawing six times, making a total of seven cycles.
Transfer the SFV dispersion into a 1 ml syringe (syringe-a) and extrude the dispersion through a 100 nm polycarbonate membrane using a LiposoFast-Basic extruder into syringe-b.
Extrude the dispersion from syringe-b back into syringe-a, then repeat the cycle ten times.
After ten cycles, remove syringe-b from the device and extrude the dispersion for the last time directly into a sterile 1.5 ml reaction tube.
Prepare a gel chromatography column using G25 beads soaked in 10 mM Tris buffer pH 7.4 (column length 28 cm, diameter 0.8 cm).
Transfer 0.5 ml of extruded vesicle dispersion onto the gel bed.
Let the sample drain into the gel matrix.
Elute the liposomes with 10 mM Tris buffer pH 7.4.
Wash the column until the free dye drains completely out of the column.
Collect and recycle the free dye by desalting and dehydration if necessary.
Concentrate the eluted liposomes by ultracentrifugation at 200,000 x g for 2 hours at 8°C.
Disperse the concentrated liposomes in an adequate volume of sterile 10 mM Tris buffer pH 7.4.
Prepare a calibration curve by dissolving DY-676-COOH in 10 mM Tris buffer containing 0.1% Triton X100 at concentrations of 0, 82, 124, 247, 494, and 988 nM.

Dissolve 2 μl (100 nmol final lipid of a 50 mmol/L stock) of the liposomes for 5 minutes at room temperature in 100 μl Tris buffer containing 1% Triton X100 to destroy vesicles and release encapsulated dye.
Dilute samples with 10 mM Tris buffer, pH 7.4 to a final Triton-X100 concentration of 0.1%, making a total volume of 1 ml.
Measure the absorption and emission of all samples (free DY-676-COOH and Triton-X100 treated liposomes) at an excitation λ=645 nm and an emission λ = 700 nm.
Establish and use a calibration curve of free dye to determine the concentration of encapsulated dye.
Determine the sizes and zeta potential of liposomes by dynamic light scattering.
Dilute liposomal samples with filter-sterilized (0.2 µm) 10 mM Tris buffer, pH 7.4, to a concentration of 100–300 µM (lipid).
Transfer diluted samples into a low volume disposable cuvette.
Measure the sample according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Characterize liposomes by electron microscopy to substantiate size, integrity, and homogeneity of liposomal vesicles according to standard protocols.
Prepare two 1.5 ml tubes for Lip-Q and two tubes for free DY-676-COOH.
Transfer 100 nmol total lipids (2.38 µl of a 42 mmol/L Lip-Q stock solution) into the corresponding tubes.
Transfer an amount of free DY-676-COOH equivalent to the dye content of Lip-Q (0.38 µg) into each tube.
Incubate one tube of each probe at 4 °C.
Freeze the second tube of each probe at -80 °C overnight (16 hr).
Heat up a heating block to 30 °C.
Fill a cooling box with crushed ice.
Equilibrate an aliquot of 10 mM Tris buffer, pH 7.4, to room temperature.
Remove probes from 4°C and equilibrate at room temperature, wrapped in aluminum foil.
Quickly thaw probes from -80°C at 30°C for 5 min.
Chill the thawed probes on ice for 1 min before transferring them to room temperature, also wrapped in aluminum foil.
Add 10 mM Tris buffer (pH 7.4) to each of the probes to achieve a final volume of 100 µl.
Equilibrate all probes at room temperature for 10 min.
Pipette 80 μl of each probe into a low volume glass cuvette.
Measure the absorption of each probe from 400–900 nm on a spectrometer.
Return the probe to their corresponding tubes.
Transfer 80 µl of each probe into a suitable glass cuvette.
Measure the fluorescence emission on a spectrofluorometer by exciting the probes at 674 nm and measuring the fluorescence from 694–800 nm.
Coat 8-well chamber slides with poly-L-lysine.
Add 100 µl of 0.001% poly-L-lysine to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the solution from each well.
Allow the chamber slides to dry up for at least 4 hours at room temperature on a sterile workbench.
Rinse the chamber slides three times with 200 µl of Hank’s buffered saline solution.
Seal the chamber slides with paraffin and aluminum foil.
Store the sealed chamber slides at 4 °C until needed.
Filter-sterilize the liposomes and dye solution.
Store the filtered solutions at 4 °C until needed.
Seed 2 x 10^6 J774A.1, U-118MG, and HT-1080 cells per culture flask with 5 ml of respective culture medium in quintuplicates.
Grow the cells for 16-24 hours.
Seed 30,000 cells of each cell line (J774A.1 and HT-1080) or 20,000 cells (U-118MG) to two wells of the chamber slide respectively.
Grow the seeded cells in 500 µl culture medium for 16-24 hours.
Add 100 nmol of Lip-Q to two flasks per cell line and one well of each cell line on the chamber slide the next day.
Immediately transfer one flask per cell line to 4 °C.
Transfer the second flask back to the incubator.
Add free DY-676-COOH at the appropriate concentration to cells in two flasks and one well per cell line on the chamber slide.
Transfer one flask per cell line immediately to 4°C for energy depletion treatment.
Incubate all treated cells for 24 hours under corresponding conditions.
Wash cells twice with Hanks buffered salt solution (HBSS) after 24-hour incubation.
Scrape cells in 500 μl HBSS and pellet by centrifugation at 200 x g for 5 minutes.
Place the tubes with cell pellets and HBSS in a NIRF imager.
Image using filters for excitation (615–665 nm) and emission (cut in >700 nm).
Deduct autofluorescence according to manufacturer instructions.
Evaluate the intensity of target versus autofluorescence.
After 24 hr incubation, harvest cells on chamber slides by washing twice with 500 µl HBSS.
Fix cells with 200 µl HBSS containing 3.7% (v/v) formaldehyde for 30 min at RT.
While fixation is going on, dilute the DNA stain, Hoechst-33258, 1:50 with mounting solution.
After fixation, wash cells twice with HBSS.
Separate the chambers from the glass slides.
Add 50 µl of mounting solution containing the DNA-stain to each spot corresponding to the wells of the chamber slides.
Cover the cells with glass coverslips.
Seal edges with transparent nail polish and air-dry for 10 min at RT (dark).
Image cells on a fluorescence microscope or confocal microscope.
Use excitation 405 nm and emission 420–480 nm for nuclei visualization with Hoechst-33258.
Use excitation 488 nm and emission 530 nm for NBD-DOPE visualization.
Use excitation 633–645 nm and emission 650–700 nm for DY-676-COOH visualization.
House 8–12 week-old male NMRI mice weighing approximately 36 g under standard conditions with food and water ad libitum.
Give all mice a low pheophorbide diet seven days prior to the start of experiments to reduce tissue autofluorescence.
Shave mice at the desired area twenty-four hours before the start of each experiment.
Weigh the animals and calculate the amount of probe to be injected per mouse (Lip-Q and Lip-dQ at 10 µmol per kg weight, free DY-676-COOH equivalent to dye content of Lip-Q used).
Image the animals in a whole body NIR Fluorescence imager with settings for cell pellets autofluorescence measurement.
Dissolve 10 mg zymosan-A in 1 ml isotonic saline solution.
Store the zymosan-A solution overnight at 4°C.
Prepare three syringes per mouse with solutions as specified.
Fill one syringe with 50 µl of a 10 mg/ml zymosan-A solution.
Fill another syringe with 50 µl isotonic saline solution.
Dilute Lip-Q and Lip-dQ to 10 µmol/kg body weight in sterile HBSS to a final volume of 150 µl.
For control animals, dilute free DY-676-COOH to the same concentration as Lip-Q in sterile HBSS to 150 µl.
Apply eye cream on the eyes of animals to prevent dryness.
Anesthetize animals with 2% isoflurane until they are deeply asleep and do not react when touched on the paws.
Place the mouse on a warm mat under anesthesia.
Inject the zymosan-A solution subcutaneously on the right hind leg.
Inject the saline solution subcutaneously on the left hind leg.
Inject the probe intravenously immediately after the subcutaneous injections.
Record time of injection/measurement as t = 0 hr.
Save resulting images as image cubes.
Image the animals every 2 hours for 10 hours post-injection and then at 24 hours post-injection.
Place a warm mat underneath the measuring chamber to avoid hypothermia during imaging.
After each measurement, place the animals in a cage with food and water ad libitum.
Place the cage in a temperate animal chamber.
Anesthetize the animals with 2% isoflurane until they no longer react to touch.
Euthanize the animals with carbon dioxide for 5-10 minutes, ensuring cessation of breathing and onset of rigor mortis.
Dissect the mice according to standard protocols.
Image the organs after dissection.
Evaluate measurement results by deducting overall fluorescence of the animals (unmixing).
Assign regions of interest for autofluorescence (left hind leg with saline) and target fluorescence of inflamed area (right hind leg with zymosan-A).
